newsitem.title: UK: OPTIONS - Options market on hold ahead of U.S data.
newsitem.headline: OPTIONS - Options market on hold ahead of U.S data.

text.p: The UK traded options market was on hold at midday as dealers awaited the U.S. unemployment figures for January, due at 1330 GMT/0830 EST.
"It hasn't been a bad morning. We've seen bits and pieces going through but things have gone quiet ahead of the U.S. numbers," one dealer said.

A put spread in Reuters Holdings Plc was established when one dealer bought 2,000 April 600 puts at 13p and at the same time sold 2,000 April 650 puts at 30p, for a net credit of 17p, less commissions.
Reuters shares were trading at 656-1/2p, up 2p, by 1250 GMT.

The dealer will make a maximum profit of 17p, the entire credit, if Reuters shares are anywhere above 650p by the time of expiration. Thus, the maximum profits if limited, regardless of how far the underlying share rises in price.
The risk is also limited in this spread strategy. The maximum loss is calculated by subtracting the net credit received from the difference in the striking prices.

In this case, if the underlying stock should decline, the spread will widen to 50 points, resulting in a maximum loss of 33p should the underlying share trade anywhere below 600p at the April expiration.
Reuters is due to publish full-year results on February 11.

Elsewhere, a reverse calendar spread was set up in BP when a dealer bought 700 April 700 calls at 50p and at the same time sold 700 July 700 calls at 63p for a net credit of 13p, less commissions. The maximum profit, which is equal to the net credit of 13p will be realised if the spread shrinks in value.

For a calendar spread to shrink, the underlying share must move far away from the striking price before the near-term call expires. The dealer makes money in this strategy if BP shares either fall well below 700p or rise well above 700p by expiration of the April call.
The maximum loss would be realised if BP was trading at exactly 700p at expiration. The near-term call would expire worthless while the long-term call, which is short, would have to be bought back.
